covered: BE94F0 constructs 34h over A5/6D/B3 patterns, preserving +25..27 and +2D..2F padding; returns owner.
BE8350 no-effect hook and BE8210 clear an unrelated nonzero publication and stamp CE3818.
BE8DF0 reserves three populated 88h records to capacity five: deep strings, all 80h payload bytes, forward old-string release; negative request clamps and leaves sufficient capacity unchanged.
BE8F30 shrinks backward after decrementing visible live count, grows within retained capacity with zero headers/payloads, and empties the vector.
BE9560 drains two feature strings, owner string, then two names in native order and clears publication/stamps base after release callbacks.
BE9600 flags zero returns the captured owner and leaves stack storage readable after full destruction.

51F460 fast path avoids an absent manager. Slow path constructs, publishes and registers once in an existing raw manager, balances a real Win32 section with captured depth seven, then takes the fast path on a second call.
normalization: String pointers are normalized to monotonic allocation identities and their length/content/terminator are compared.
Owner/vector backing pointers are normalized to null/non-null because the unchanged source allocator uses the current CRT.
All 52 owner bytes are compared in patterned ctor/destructor cases after pointer normalization. Only the six unwritten malloc padding bytes are excluded for slow-getter storage.
String-release trace records allocation identity, size, observed feature/name counts, owner profile and publication presence.
boundaries: No original FH3/SEH exception path, failing allocation/registration, reentrant publication changes, hardware faults, or native register-level no-op EAX identity is exercised.
Raw manager getter/registration, source string/string-vector helpers, allocation/free/memmove/memset and Win32 imports are shared explicit support, not original dependencies independently compared.
The fixture supplies NativeStringStorage allocation/release observation; it does not compare the actual game pool implementation.
Payload arrays are disjoint; REP MOVSD forward-overlap behavior remains assembly evidence, not a runtime overlap result.
Flags-one owner free, heap backing-free identity/order, and central D68B94 mixed-owner drain binding are outside these assertions.
This is a bounded source-interface fixture, not drop-in ABI compatibility, original complete startup, or game validation.
